requirements.text: Every source file MUST carry an SPDX-License-Identifier header matching its plane.
Apache-2.0 code MUST NOT include, vendor, statically link, or #include any header from a GPL-licensed work. Not once, not "temporarily".

CI MUST run a licence-lint job that fails the build on any violation of REQ-LIC-1 or REQ-LIC-2, including transitive dependencies. Contributor confusion is the main practical risk of a split licence, so the mitigation is mechanical rather than documentary.
The engine MUST ship as a standalone executable that is independently useful and independently runnable.
A conforming alternative engine MUST remain possible. The stub engine (§2.9) exists permanently to prove this and MUST stay green in CI.
FFmpeg MUST be built LGPL-only, with enabled components audited in CI. A GPL-configured build silently relicenses the product.
Third-party dependency licences MUST be inventoried in a generated NOTICE file per release artifact.
The Apache-2.0 venue layer and the GPL engine MUST be released as separate artifacts. They MUST NOT be distributed together in a single installer, archive, container image or package (ADR-006).
Contributions MUST be accepted under a DCO with inbound=outbound licensing, so the single-GPL fallback in ADR-006 remains exercisable without tracing every contributor (ADR-006).
Transport MUST be a local stream socket: Unix domain socket on POSIX, named pipe on Windows. TCP on loopback MAY be offered for development, MUST be off by default.
Framing MUST be newline-delimited JSON (one object per line, UTF-8).
The protocol MUST NOT use shared memory or pass structures whose layout is defined by GPL headers. Arms-length generality is a licence requirement (ADR-001), not a style preference.
The engine MUST accept multiple concurrent clients and MUST apply per-client subscription state independently.
Group names MUST be stable across engine restarts.
Deck groups MUST be [Channel1]…[ChannelN]; the master bus MUST be [Master].
Receivers MUST ignore unknown object fields, so the protocol can extend without a version bump.
Every error MUST carry a machine-readable code from a documented enumeration.
The protocol MUST be versioned cdep/<major>. Breaking changes bump the major.
The engine MUST reject an unsupported protocol version with unsupported_protocol and close the connection.

welcome MUST advertise optional features in capabilities. Clients MUST degrade gracefully when a capability is absent — this is what allows the stub engine to be conformant while implementing far less than the Mixxx engine.

describe MUST return every control with a descriptor carrying group, item, default, readonly, and a human label. type (bool | int | float | enum), min and max are SHOULD — an engine supplies them where it knows them and omits them where it does not.

Every control MUST additionally be readable and writable in parameter space: a normalised 0.0..1.0 where 0 is the control's minimum useful position and 1 its maximum. get MUST return parameter alongside value; set MUST accept either.

The description MUST be sufficient to build a complete control UI and a complete MIDI-mapping target list with no hard-coded knowledge of the engine. A client that uses only parameter space MUST be able to do this using solely MUST-level descriptor fields.
subscribe MUST accept max_hz and the engine MUST coalesce updates to that rate, emitting only the latest value per control per interval.
High-rate controls (playposition, VU meters) MUST NOT be delivered unsubscribed.

If a client's send queue exceeds a bounded depth, the engine MUST drop coalesced updates rather than block. The audio thread MUST NEVER block on IPC — this is the hard rule the whole two-plane split exists to guarantee.
A published conformance suite MUST exist, and both engine/ and engine-stub/ MUST pass it in CI.

engine-stub/ MUST implement: handshake, describe, get/set, subscribe/changed, load, transport, and gapless sequential playback — enough for the fusion core to be developed and tested against it with no Mixxx dependency.
Every queue entry MUST occupy exactly one state, and transitions MUST be recorded with a timestamp and actor.
requested → screened MUST be performed by the policy engine (§3.5). An entry failing policy MUST go to rejected with a machine-readable reason.
In attended mode, staged → cued MUST require an explicit DJ action.
In autonomous mode, screened → staged → cued MUST proceed automatically.
Patrons MUST NOT be able to cause a cued or playing entry to change state. Only staff and the engine may.
Staff-pinned entries MUST sort above all others regardless of score.
The ordering function MUST treat votes and boost units as two inputs to one score, so that enabling payments in v1.1 requires no scheduler change (ADR-003).
age_bonus MUST be non-zero and monotonically increasing. Without an aging term an unpopular request never plays; anti-starvation is a correctness property, not a nicety.
All weights and intervals MUST be venue-configurable, with documented defaults (VOTE_WEIGHT=10, BOOST_WEIGHT=25, AGING_INTERVAL=5min, AGING_WEIGHT=3).
priority_score MUST be recomputed deterministically; identical inputs give identical ordering. It MUST NOT depend on wall-clock time except through age_bonus.
Every patron MUST see their entry's 1-based position in the effective play order. This is TouchTunes' single most-cited feature and is what makes waiting tolerable.
Position MUST update in real time over WebSocket when the ordering changes.
An estimated time-until-play SHOULD be derived from queued track durations.
max_pending_per_patron (default 2) MUST be enforced at request time.
track_cooldown (default 60 min) and artist_cooldown (default 30 min) MUST block re-requests venue-wide, counting from last play.
A per-patron request rate limit (default 5 per 15 min) MUST apply.
A patron MUST NOT vote twice for the same entry, enforced by a uniqueness constraint rather than UI logic.
Every rejection MUST return a specific reason so the client can explain it.
Requests MUST be screened against: explicit-content flag, artist/genre block lists, allow-list mode, per-daypart rules, and licence class (§4.4).
Patron search MUST be scoped by the same policy, so an unrequestable track is never offered. Filtering only at request time is a defect.
Policy MUST be evaluated at request time and re-evaluated at cued, since dayparting may have changed in between.
Staff MUST be able to override any policy decision, and the override MUST be logged.
The venue MUST be in exactly one mode: autonomous or attended.
Mode transitions MUST NOT interrupt audio. A track playing across a handoff continues.
Entering attended MUST stop automatic staged → cued promotion, leaving already cued entries intact.
Entering autonomous MUST resume automatic promotion from the current queue state.
In autonomous, the engine MUST beatmatch transitions using the analysed beatgrid, falling back to a timed crossfade when confidence is low.
When the queue empties, the scheduler MUST promote from a configured fallback source (playlist, smart playlist, or CC catalog).
Fallback selections MUST pass the same policy screening.
Dead air MUST NOT exceed 2 seconds under any queue state, including at venue open, after a skip, and on engine reconnect.
If the engine connection drops, the fusion core MUST reconnect with backoff and resume from persisted queue state. The queue is durable; the engine is replaceable.
Every venue-scoped table MUST carry venue_id from the first migration, even though v1 binds to one venue (ADR-004). Near-zero cost now; a migration across every table and query later.
The runtime MUST bind to exactly one venue_id. Cross-venue queries are out of scope.
The ledger MUST be append-only. Corrections are compensating entries, never updates.
Balance MUST be derived as the sum of deltas, never stored as a mutable column.
v1 MUST accept reason values staff_grant, promotion, spend, refund only. No paid top-up path exists in v1.
Credits MUST NOT expire (matching the TouchTunes wallet mechanic).
Spending credits MUST be atomic with the boost it purchases; a failed boost MUST NOT consume credit.
Every track MUST carry a licence_class: owned_local, cc_attribution, cc_sharealike, cc_noncommercial, record_pool, licensed_stream, unknown.
The system MUST be able to answer "may this venue legally play this track now?" from licence_class + venue_licence_profile.
cc_noncommercial and unknown MUST default to blocked in a commercial venue profile.
Attribution-required tracks MUST surface attribution on the venue display while playing.
Every performance MUST be logged with start, end, mode and licence class.
The log MUST be exportable as CSV for PRO reporting.
The log MUST be local-only and MUST NOT be transmitted anywhere.
The API MUST be the only way clients interact with the system. No privileged back door for first-party consoles — this is what makes third-party clients viable.
Paths MUST be namespaced /v1/venues/{venue_id}/... from the start (ADR-004), so client URLs survive the move to federation.
All mutations MUST be authenticated; patron auth is a venue-scoped session token bound to a QR join.
The API MUST be documented as OpenAPI 3.1, generated in CI.
Staff actions MUST be logged to queue_entry_event with the actor.
POST /panic MUST stop output within 500 ms.
The DJ console MUST drive the engine through the core, not by connecting to CDEP directly — one authority over deck state.
Deck state MUST stream over WebSocket at a coalesced rate suitable for UI (≥20 Hz for playposition).
The DJ console MUST be served locally by the appliance and MUST function with no WAN connectivity.
The appliance MUST expose an OpenSubsonic-compatible subset at /rest/: ping, getLicense, search3, getAlbumList2, getPlaylists, stream, getCoverArt.

jukeboxControl MUST be implemented. Its playlist MUST be able to represent queue entries that are not Subsonic library songs — a Creative Commons provider track, or a live MIDI instrument (REQ-INST-1) — because a queue that can only express song IDs cannot describe this product's queue.

That capability MUST be advertised through getOpenSubsonicExtensions under a vendor-namespaced name, and entries a stock client cannot understand MUST still be returned as valid Child objects, so an unmodified Subsonic client shows a coherent queue rather than failing.

Subsonic-authenticated clients MUST be treated as staff-level, since the Subsonic auth model has no patron concept. The Subsonic surface MUST be disabled unless explicitly configured with its own credential, and that credential MUST NOT default to the staff key.
The engine MUST support MIDI 1.0 and MIDI 2.0/UMP via libremidi, with RtMidi as a fallback backend behind our own port interface.

Ports MUST be identified by a stable identity (manufacturer, product, serial where available) and MUST NOT be bound by numeric index. Index-bound mappings break on reboot — this is a known defect class in existing tools and we design it out.
Hot-plug attach/detach MUST be handled without restart, and mappings MUST re-bind automatically on reattach.
MIDI learn MUST support soft-takeover: a physical control MUST NOT apply its value until it crosses the current software value, preventing parameter jumps.

The mapping format MUST be declarative, human-readable, diffable and shareable, and MUST target controls by CDEP (group, item) — so the mapping target list is generated from describe (REQ-CDEP-13) with no hard-coded engine knowledge.
A mapping MUST be exportable and importable as a single file.
HID SHOULD be supported for high-resolution jog wheels; 7-bit MIDI's 128 steps per rotation is insufficient for credible feel.
Where a device supports MIDI-CI, the system SHOULD use Property Exchange to auto-populate a mapping, reducing hand-authoring.
Auto-generated mappings MUST be editable and MUST be overridable by a user mapping.
The leader deck MUST be the single tempo source, publishing to MIDI Clock and Ableton Link simultaneously.
MIDI Clock MUST be emitted at 24 PPQN.
Ableton Link MUST support a configurable quantum and enableStartStopSync.
Clock MUST continue across a mode handoff (§3.6) — external instruments MUST NOT lose sync when a DJ takes over or steps away.
MTC MUST NOT be used for musical sync; positional reference only.
Clock jitter MUST be ≤1 ms RMS measured at the MIDI output.
A live MIDI instrument input MUST be registrable as a queueable source, so it can be scheduled in the queue like a track. This is the brief's distinguishing idea taken to its conclusion.
An instrument entry MUST have a staff-set duration or an explicit end action, and MUST obey never-silent fallback (REQ-FALL-3) if it ends early.
Local ingest MUST tag via MusicBrainz with Chromaprint/AcoustID fingerprinting, and MUST de-duplicate by fingerprint.
Ingest MUST produce the analysis cache in one pass: beatgrid, key, loudness, waveform, phrases.
Analysis MUST run out-of-process; it MUST NOT share a process with the audio engine.
Loudness MUST be normalised (ReplayGain / EBU R128) across all sources. Mixing a CC track, a local file and a live instrument without this is unacceptable in a venue.
Provider adapters MUST implement one interface: search, resolve, stream URL, licence class.
v1 MUST ship local, opensubsonic and at least one CC provider (Jamendo), so a fresh install has legally playable music on first run.

The system MUST NOT include any adapter sourcing venue playback from a consumer streaming account or a media downloader (H4, ADR-003 rationale). This is the flaw that makes the existing open-source jukeboxes unusable in venues, and it is designed out rather than documented around.
The audio thread MUST NOT allocate, lock, log, or perform I/O.
Audio buffer xruns MUST be counted and surfaced as a CDEP event.
The appliance MUST be fully functional with no WAN connectivity — the single clearest advantage over cloud jukeboxes, whose music stops when the venue's connection drops.
Queue state MUST survive process restart.
A fusion-core crash MUST NOT stop audio; the engine continues its cued track and the core resumes on reconnect.
No telemetry. The system MUST NOT transmit usage data anywhere by default.
Patron sessions MUST be venue-scoped, expiring, and MUST NOT require personal data.
Staff endpoints MUST require a separate credential from patron sessions.
Outbound network access MUST be limited to enabled providers and MUST be disable-able entirely.
A single-command container deploy MUST bring up a working appliance.
Target baseline hardware: 4-core x86-64 or ARM64, 8 GB RAM, no GPU. Stem separation is explicitly not required for v1, so no GPU dependency exists.

acceptance.text: Given attended mode and a screened request, when it reaches the staging lane, then it MUST NOT become audible until a DJ promotes it.
Given autonomous mode and ≥2 queued tracks with confident beatgrids, when one ends, then the next is beatmatched in with no gap.
Given a track playing in autonomous mode, when a DJ switches to attended, then audio continues uninterrupted and auto-promotion stops.
Given a patron with a queued request, when the ordering changes, then their displayed position updates within 250 ms without a page reload.
Given max_pending_per_patron=2, when a patron submits a third request, then it is rejected with reason patron_limit.
Given a track played 10 minutes ago and a 60-minute cooldown, when any patron requests it, then it is rejected with reason track_cooldown.
Given explicit content is disallowed, when a patron searches, then explicit tracks appear in neither results nor request attempts.
Given an empty queue, when the current track ends, then a fallback track begins within 2 seconds.
Given any playback state, when staff trigger panic, then output stops within 500 ms and the event is logged.
Given a mapped controller, when it is unplugged and replugged, then the mapping re-binds automatically with no restart.
Given a physical fader at 0.0 and software at 0.8, when the fader is moved, then the value does not jump — it engages only on crossing 0.8.
Given an external instrument slaved to MIDI Clock, when leader-deck tempo changes, then the instrument follows within one beat and ≤1 ms RMS jitter.
Given WAN is disconnected, when the full day-in-the-life scenario (§0.4) runs, then every step succeeds.
Given a cc_noncommercial track and a commercial venue profile, when it is requested, then it is rejected with reason licence_class.
Given a folder of untagged audio, when ingest runs, then every file is fingerprint-identified, de-duplicated, and has a complete analysis cache.
Given the repository, when CI licence-lint runs, then it fails if any GPL header is reachable from Apache-2.0 code.
Given the CDEP conformance suite, when it runs against both engines, then both pass.
Given a client that stops reading its socket, when high-rate updates are produced, then updates are dropped and audio is unaffected.
